results.criterion: AC1: Both commands require the selected Project, saved plan, matching explicitly approved digest and current approved/in-progress shared Quick Task authority. Draft, terminal, foreign, revoked or owner-local records cannot authorize migration; bootstrap resolution does not require the catalog being established.
results.observation: Foreign-qualified, draft and terminal task references deny execution; approved shared authority is resolved live, including authorized progress on completed rerun.

results.criterion: AC2: Apply recomputes the canonical plan with saved inputs/assignments and checks complete source inventory, hashes, candidate bytes and destination state. Ambiguity, tampering, missing/new records, drift, collisions, traversal, symlink components and non-regular files reject without changing authoritative records.
results.observation: Added and changed inputs, rehashed fabricated candidates, occupied targets and symlinked plan/destination cases reject without overwriting source or outside files.

results.criterion: AC3: The staged candidate passes `SpecCatalog.validate` and intended live-link checks before authoritative mutation. New owner entries/indexes and record identities are correct; old feature files are removed only through checked operations.
results.observation: Actual API/CLI migration produces validated owner entries, indexes and qualified local/cross-owner dependencies; original flat source files are removed.

results.criterion: AC4: Under the existing creation lock, durable before images and ordered intent/result records precede each publication/deletion. Ordinary injected failure restores original affected bytes; unrelated work is unchanged and the Project root and lock remain intact.
results.observation: Injected failure restores source bytes, prior bound STATUS and transaction-created directories; immutable history remains unchanged.

results.criterion: AC5: Actual subprocess interruption at intent/publication boundaries leaves a recognizable incomplete transaction. Explicit recovery reconciles recorded hashes, restores incomplete application or verifies/finalizes complete output; external edits cause a conflict instead of being overwritten. A second transaction refuses while recovery is required.
results.observation: Real subprocess crash/recover/retry works; external edits are preserved as conflicts; recovery finalizes the abandoned managed candidate run.

results.criterion: AC6: A successful receipt records Project identity, exact plan/work-record identities, old-to-new mapping, input/output hashes, fingerprint review requirements and STATUS disposition. It is written last and is not work-completion authority.
results.observation: Actual repository CLI receipt original-source SHA-256 was independently checked; receipts include complete inputs, before/after outputs and old-to-new mapping and remain separate from completion authority.

results.criterion: AC7: Repeating the same completed plan verifies its receipt/output hashes and makes no new content changes, owners or receipts. Completed-output drift reports a conflict rather than overwriting later work.
results.observation: Completed cutover without receipt is finalized by recovery; repeating apply returns identical receipt and unchanged content; legitimate task progress is accepted.

results.criterion: AC8: Bound external STATUS belongs to the transaction and rollback; an unbound Project remains unbound. Lifecycle decisions, immutable evidence/log bytes and historical completion semantics are preserved without minted approvals.
results.observation: Missing STATUS at an existing bound root is created from the exact reviewed bytes; existing STATUS rollback and unbound disposition were exercised; migration does not install adapters.

results.criterion: AC9: Actual apply/recover CLI smoke and permanent state-transition regressions prove success, rejection, ordinary rollback, interruption recovery and idempotence; focused checks pass and code receives independent review.
results.observation: Real command smoke, 48 focused checks and 15-module suite passed; converged Standards/Spec review is recorded.
